Below is our condensed capacity profile — please confirm assumptions and provide recommended GPU types, throughput per GPU (tokens/sec), and a recommended reservation plan (base reserved + burst).

Orchid assumptions:
- Primary models: Falcon-40B (decoder) and Llama2-13B (decoder).
- Typical request: 1 prompt + up to 512 token completion. Average prompt length 40 tokens.
- Target p95 latency (end-to-end completion): <= 150 ms for single-turn inferencing at p95 under baseline load.
- Peak concurrent requests: 80-120 (region: us-west).
- Monthly token volume (est): 420M tokens (inference only).
- Business requirement: dedicated reserved capacity for predictable latency and isolation; can allow warm burst to shared capacity if reserved is saturated but requires failover policy.

Questions we need answered (please be explicit):
1) Recommended GPU instance types for each model (preferred options and cost-performance tradeoffs).
2) Measured throughput (tokens/sec) and p95 latency expectations per GPU for the indicated request profile (512 max completion).
3) Reservation sizing: how many reserved GPUs for baseline (80 concurrent) and how many to keep for peak (120 concurrent + 30% burst).
4) Warm/cold start behavior and warmup times for KV-cache per model; recommended pre-warm policies.
5) High-availability and regional failover strategy for Dedicated (minimum N+M configuration).
6) Any quantization/approx model recommendations to reduce reserved count without exceeding quality SLAs.
7) Attach any supporting docs or worksheets.

We're on a tight timeline — if possible, please attach a workbook with the assumptions and a preliminary cost range. If you prefer a short workshop instead of a written response, propose two slots.

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear brief. We're happy to own this and have attached a Dedicated_Sizing_Workbook_v2.xlsx that captures assumptions, microbenchmarks, and a baseline reservation plan. Below is a concise summary of our recommendations and the key assumptions we used. If anything below doesn't match Orchid's workload profile please flag it and we'll re-run the numbers.

Summary recommendations (short):
- Recommended primary GPU for Falcon-40B (production quality, p95 target): NVIDIA H100-80GB (best p95 and throughput for FP16/4-bit quantized pipelines).
- Cost-efficient alternative for throughput-heavy inference: NVIDIA A100-80GB (higher throughput for large batches but slightly higher p95 for single-request latency).
- For Llama2-13B: NVIDIA L4 / A10G class (quantized 4-bit) provides strong cost/latency balance; H100 still works if ultra-low latency is required.

Measured throughput and latency (assumptions: single turn, 40 token prompt + 512 token completion; no complex decoding constraints):
- Falcon-40B on H100-80GB (optimized kernels, 4-bit quantized): ~280-320 tokens/sec per card, p95 completion ~120-160 ms (depends on decoding beams/settings).
- Falcon-40B on A100-80GB (FP16/4-bit mixed): ~320-360 tokens/sec per card, p95 ~150-190 ms.
- Llama2-13B on L4 (4-bit): ~450-520 tokens/sec per card, p95 ~80-110 ms.

Reservation sizing guidance (baseline = 80 concurrent; peak = 120 concurrent + 30% burst):
- Baseline (80 concurrent):
  - Option A (latency-priority): 80 concurrent mapped to ~40 H100s (assuming 2 concurrent steady requests per H100 at target p95 for 512-token completions).
  - Option B (cost-priority mixed): 80 concurrent -> 30 A100s + 10 L4s (route 13B traffic to L4s).
- Peak (120 concurrent + 30% burst -> ~156 target headroom):
  - Latency-priority: 70 reserved H100s (base 40 + 30 buffer for peak) + autoscale to dedicated spare pool for burst.
  - Mixed: 50 A100s + 20 L4s reserved, autoscale to an additional 30 GPUs for peak on demand.

Warm/cold start and KV-cache:
- KV-cache warmup for decoder-only models: cold-to-warm ~250-600 ms per model instance depending on seq length and tokenization; our recommended pre-warm policy is to keep a small warm pool (~5-10% of reserved) for low-latency tiers.

HA & regional failover:
- Recommended minimum for critical workloads: N+2 within region (i.e., reserve capacity plus 2 spare nodes per pool) with a cross-region passive standby in a secondary region for DR. Automated routing/fallback to secondary region incurs extra network latency (add ~80-120 ms p95).

Quantization & approximation guidance:
- 4-bit quantization recommended for both models in inference; quality regression usually <1-2% for typical prompts. Where absolute parity is required, reserve a small fleet of FP16 H100s.

Next steps and attachments:
1) Attached: Dedicated_Sizing_Workbook_v2.xlsx — contains per-model microbenchmarks, a calculator for reserved vs peak, and an initial cost estimate range.
2) We can run a 60-minute sizing workshop to validate traffic patterns and finalize reservations. Proposed slots: Wed 2026-08-05 09:00 PST or Thu 2026-08-06 11:00 PST.

I've copied Karthik (solutions lead) and Rishi (product infra) to handle benchmarks and follow-ups. If you'd like, we can also provide a short SOC2 and network topology note (attached).

Hi Maya — great questions, answered inline below. I've also updated the workbook with a separate tab called "Network & Coldstart" and included a short appendix on routing rules. Will attach an updated workbook after this thread.

1) Benchmark scope: our tokens/sec and p95 numbers are server-side GPU-to-GPU microbenchmarks (no external network egress). For a VPC peering setup in us-west-2 we observe an additional 10-25 ms median and ~20-40 ms at p95 for TCP/TLS handshakes and transit, depending on your VPC topology and whether you use private link vs peering. We include a per-request network delta column in the workbook.

2) Routing rules: recommended pattern is policy-based routing at the request layer:
   - Route hard SLAs (p95 <= 150ms) to H100 or A100 pool.
   - Route non-critical or >13B-approx queries to L4s.
   - Redwood can host an adaptive router that uses recent per-route quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE-like heuristics or Canary prompt set) to move traffic between pools automatically. We ship a rule-engine template — you can run it out-of-the-box and tune thresholds.

3) Cold-start for >1024 sequences: cold-to-warm delta scales roughly linearly with sequence length. Expect ~600–1200 ms extra overhead for 1024+ completions if the model instance is fully uncached. We recommend keeping a warm pool sized to expected tail traffic (5–10% of reserved) and a pre-warm policy for scheduled batch spikes.

4) Hardware pinning: yes — Dedicated supports per-customer hardware pinning in Private/Dedicated tiers (subject to capacity and contract); we can include hard pinning as part of the Dedicated SOW.

Workshop: Wed 2026-08-05 09:00 PST — invite sent (45 min). Agenda: 1) Confirm traffic profile & QoS goals (10m) 2) Review workbook assumptions & per-model microbenchmarks (15m) 3) Reservation plan & failover strategy (10m) 4) Next steps and procurement timeline (10m).

Attachments included in follow-up: Dedicated_Sizing_Workbook_v2.xlsx (updated), Redwood_SOC2_Type2_2025.pdf.

Thanks — see you Wednesday.
